what-is-flask-commands.title: What is Flask-Commands
what-is-flask-commands.description: Learn what Flask-Commands is built to do, which parts of a Flask app it accelerates, and why the project leans so hard into local-first scaffolding.

what-flask-commands-is-not.title: What Flask-Commands is not
what-flask-commands-is-not.description: Learn what the tool is intentionally not trying to solve so you can keep your expectations aimed at structure, wiring, and repeatable setup instead of design polish.

the-plain-recipe-app-we-are-building.title: The plain recipe app we are building
the-plain-recipe-app-we-are-building.description: Learn why the docs use a plain recipe app as the teaching example and how that example gives us believable nested relationships to work with.

how-to-use-this-documentation.title: How to Use This Documentation
how-to-use-this-documentation.description: Learn how the written chapters and video callouts fit together so you can follow the course in order or jump to the command family you need.

install-the-prerequisites-for-flask-comm.title: Install The Prerequisites for Flask-Commands
install-the-prerequisites-for-flask-comm.description: Learn which local tools Flask-Commands expects, why pipx and npm matter, and how to check that your machine is ready before installing the package.

install-flask-commands-with-pipx.title: Install Flask-Commands with pipx
install-flask-commands-with-pipx.description: Learn the recommended install path for keeping the Flask-Commands plugins available globally without mixing the package into a project environment.

install-flask-commands-with-pip.title: Install Flask-Commands with pip
install-flask-commands-with-pip.description: Learn the plain pip installation path, when it is acceptable, and what tradeoffs it has compared to the recommended pipx setup.

confirm-the-command-with-version.title: Confirm the command with version
confirm-the-command-with-version.description: Learn how to verify that Flask-Commands is installed through Flask's CLI using `flask commands --version`, and how that differs from `flask --version`.

read-the-cli-at-a-glance-with-help.title: Read the CLI at a glance with help
read-the-cli-at-a-glance-with-help.description: See how Flask-Commands appears inside Flask's help output, and how to find specific Flask-Commands help documentation.

create-a-project-with-flask-new.title: Create a project with flask new
create-a-project-with-flask-new.description: Watch the first project scaffold come together so you can see the shape of the generated app before drilling into each file and folder in later chapters.

what-the-default-scaffold-gives-you.title: What the default scaffold gives you
what-the-default-scaffold-gives-you.description: Learn what the default project structure includes out of the box so you know which files, folders, and moving parts Flask-Commands is creating for you.

create-a-project-without-a-database.title: Create a project without a database
create-a-project-without-a-database.description: Learn when the no-database project path is the better fit and what changes when you ask the scaffold to leave the database pieces out.

run-the-new-project.title: Run the new project
run-the-new-project.description: Watch the new project come to life so you can connect the generated files on disk to the running app in the browser.

project-root-safety.title: Project-root safety
project-root-safety.description: Learn why the generators only run inside a valid Flask-Commands project and how that safeguard helps prevent confusing writes in the wrong directory.

restful-actions.title: RESTful actions
restful-actions.description: Learn the RESTful action names the package leans on and why those names matter for predictable routes, controllers, and views.

dot-notation.title: Dot notation
dot-notation.description: Learn how dotted input maps cleanly onto folders, route namespaces, and nested app structure as the project grows.

naming-conventions.title: Naming conventions
naming-conventions.description: Learn the naming patterns the generators expect so your controllers, models, routes, and templates line up without extra translation work.

view-input-normalization.title: Input normalization
view-input-normalization.description: Learn how Flask-Commands cleans up and interprets your input before scaffolding so the commands feel forgiving without becoming mysterious.

into-to-flask-make-view.title: Intro to flask make:view
into-to-flask-make-view.description: Learn what `flask make:view` does in broad terms, why it is such a useful page-first starting point, and how the command can grow from a simple template into fuller application structure.

create-a-simple-template-with-flask-make.title: Create a simple template with flask make:view
create-a-simple-template-with-flask-make.description: Watch the smallest useful make:view example so you can see how fast the page-first workflow gets a template and route onto the screen.

understand-the-mains-namespace.title: Understand the mains namespace
understand-the-mains-namespace.description: Learn what the mains namespace is doing for you and when it is perfectly reasonable to keep simple pages there on purpose.

wire-a-page-explicitly.title: Wire a page explicitly
wire-a-page-explicitly.description: Learn how to create a page with clearer intent so the route, view file, and structure are obvious from the command you ran.

use-generator-flags-with-make-view.title: Use generator flags with make:view
use-generator-flags-with-make-view.description: Learn which flags add route, controller, and model wiring so you can choose the smallest or largest scaffold that fits the job.

use-mains-intentionally.title: Use mains intentionally
use-mains-intentionally.description: Learn when staying in mains keeps the app simple and when that simplicity is a feature instead of a sign that you are doing something wrong.

a-quick-peek-at-nested-views.title: A quick peek at nested views
a-quick-peek-at-nested-views.description: Watch the nested-view workflow at a high level so you can see how dot notation grows into folders and clearer page structure.

when-make-view-is-the-right-starting-poi.title: When make:view is the right starting point
when-make-view-is-the-right-starting-poi.description: Learn when the page-first workflow is the easiest way to start, especially when you want to see interface structure before deeper controller or model work.

normalize-input-before-scaffolding.title: Normalize input before scaffolding
normalize-input-before-scaffolding.description: Learn how the command cleans up dotted paths and action names before writing files so your intent survives small formatting differences.

understand-missing-model-prompts.title: Understand missing-model prompts
understand-missing-model-prompts.description: Learn why Flask-Commands asks about models in some view workflows and what that prompt is trying to protect or accelerate.

avoid-prompts-with-flags.title: Avoid prompts with flags
avoid-prompts-with-flags.description: Learn how to steer the generator directly when you already know the route or model behavior you want and do not need interactive help.

choose-between-route-model-and-m.title: Choose between --route, --model, and -m
choose-between-route-model-and-m.description: Learn what each flag is responsible for so you can be more explicit about whether you are wiring routes, generating a model, or both.

model-prompts-final-comment.title: Model Prompts Final Comment
model-prompts-final-comment.description: Learn the design goal behind the make:view model prompts so the command feels helpful when you need guidance and quiet when you already know the answer.

get-actions-render-pages.title: Get Actions Render Pages
get-actions-render-pages.description: Learn why RESTful GET actions create templates, which actions belong in that group, and how Flask-Commands maps page-rendering behavior to files.

post-actions-change-state.title: Post Actions Change State
post-actions-change-state.description: Learn why POST-style RESTful actions change application state instead of rendering their own templates, and why redirects are the right generated behavior.

the-browser-flow.title: The Browser Flow
the-browser-flow.description: See the normal GET, POST, redirect loop that connects form pages, submissions, and follow-up pages in a traditional Flask browser workflow.

a-real-example-with-recipes-create-and-r.title: A Real Example With Recipes Create And Recipe Store
a-real-example-with-recipes-create-and-r.description: Walk through recipes.create and recipes.store as a paired example so the difference between showing a form and processing that form becomes concrete.

no-template-for-post-actions.title: No Template For Post Actions
no-template-for-post-actions.description: Learn why commands such as recipes.store generate route and controller wiring without creating a template file, and why that is intentional.

what-get-vs-post-means-when-using-make-v.title: What Get vs Post Means When Using Make View
what-get-vs-post-means-when-using-make-v.description: Learn how to predict make:view output by asking whether the action should display a page or process submitted data and redirect.

get-templates-vs-post-actions.title: GET templates vs POST actions
get-templates-vs-post-actions.description: Learn why some actions produce templates and others do not, and how that distinction keeps the generated files honest to HTTP behavior.

why-the-smarter-behavior-matters.title: Why the smarter behavior matters
why-the-smarter-behavior-matters.description: Learn how the newer scaffolding behavior reduces manual cleanup by making better guesses before it writes your files.

build-recipes-index-as-the-first-resourc.title: Build recipes.index as the first resource
build-recipes-index-as-the-first-resourc.description: Watch the first real resource come together so you can see routes, controllers, models, and templates start acting like one connected feature.

understand-what-rcm-created.title: Understand what -rcm created
understand-what-rcm-created.description: Learn how to read the generated output from a combined scaffold command so you know exactly which files were created and why.

add-recipes-show-to-the-resource.title: Add recipes.show to the resource
add-recipes-show-to-the-resource.description: Watch the second RESTful page slot into the existing resource so you can feel how the structure starts paying off after the first scaffold.

why-recipes-show-matters.title: Why recipes.show matters
why-recipes-show-matters.description: Learn why the show page is such an important step in making a resource feel real instead of just looking like a list on the screen.

keep-the-templates-intentionally-plain.title: Keep the templates intentionally plain
keep-the-templates-intentionally-plain.description: Learn why the docs keep the early templates visually simple so the real lesson stays on data shape, routing, and structure.

with-two-commands-you-have-something-to-.title: With Two Commands You Have Something To Show
with-two-commands-you-have-something-to-.description: See how recipes.index and recipes.show give you the beginning of a real resource with list and detail pages connected to the generated structure.

build-recipes-comments-index.title: Build recipes.comments.index
build-recipes-comments-index.description: Watch the first nested resource step appear under a parent so you can see how truthful dotted naming turns into working nested structure.

add-recipes-comments-show.title: Add recipes.comments.show
add-recipes-comments-show.description: Learn how a nested show page fits beside a nested index page and why that symmetry helps the structure stay understandable.

go-three-levels-deep-with-images.title: Go three levels deep with images
go-three-levels-deep-with-images.description: Watch the nesting go one level further so you can see how the package handles deeper relationships without hiding what is happening.

why-nesting-pays-off.title: Why Nesting Pays Off
why-nesting-pays-off.description: Learn how a few nested make:view commands create relationship-aware routes, controllers, templates, and endpoint names that stay readable as the app grows.

intro-to-flask-make-controller.title: Intro To Flask Make Controller
intro-to-flask-make-controller.description: Learn when it makes sense to start from controller behavior and how make:controller helps scaffold the layer that coordinates routes, templates, and models.

create-a-simple-controller.title: Create a simple controller
create-a-simple-controller.description: Learn how to start with the controller layer directly when the behavior feels clearer than the page or model structure at the beginning.

add-restful-actions-with-crud.title: Add RESTful actions with --crud
add-restful-actions-with-crud.description: Learn how the controller generator expands into a full RESTful action set so you can scaffold behavior in one pass instead of method by method.

why-crud-feels-like-a-big-deal.title: Why --crud Feels Like A Big Deal
why-crud-feels-like-a-big-deal.description: Learn why the --crud flag is such a useful jump in scaffolding power when you want the full RESTful controller, route, and template shape at once.

add-a-model-with-model-or-m.title: Add a model with --model or -m
add-a-model-with-model-or-m.description: Learn the difference between the explicit long flag and the shorthand model-generation path so the command does exactly what you intend.

name-the-model-directly.title: Name the Model Directly
name-the-model-directly.description: Learn how --model lets you choose the exact model name instead of asking Flask-Commands to infer one from the controller name.

generate-the-model-name.title: Generate the Model Name
generate-the-model-name.description: Learn how -m asks Flask-Commands to generate a model name from the controller name and when that shorthand is clear enough to use.

why-both-options-matter.title: Why Both Options Matter
why-both-options-matter.description: Learn why explicit model naming and generated model naming both matter once controller names start carrying namespaces, multi-word models, or relationships.

generating-a-restful-controller-with-a-m.title: Generating a RESTful Controller with a Model
generating-a-restful-controller-with-a-m.description: Watch --crud and -m work together to create a RESTful controller, routes, templates, and a registered model from one controller-first command.

the-naming-problem.title: The Naming Problem
the-naming-problem.description: Learn the three naming stories Flask-Commands has to separate: one multi-word data structure, a namespace, and a nested resource relationship.

single-data-structures-that-are-multiple.title: Single Data Structures that are Multiple Words
single-data-structures-that-are-multiple.description: Learn how to keep names like ShoppingList together as one model-backed resource instead of accidentally turning the words into nested structure.

when-to-namespace.title: When to Namespace
when-to-namespace.description: Learn when a leading name segment is better understood as an organizing namespace rather than a model or parent resource.

multi-word-namespaces.title: Multi-Word Namespaces
multi-word-namespaces.description: Learn how multi-word namespaces map to route packages, endpoint names, and URLs while staying separate from the model name itself.

public-pages-and-private-tools.title: Public Pages and Private Tools
public-pages-and-private-tools.description: Learn how namespaces can separate public resource pages from private tool surfaces that manage the same underlying model.

naming-nested-controllers-by-relationshi.title: Naming Nested Controllers by Relationship
naming-nested-controllers-by-relationshi.description: Learn how nested controller names describe parent-child relationships and how that relationship appears in generated routes and folders.

go-nested-with-make-controller-crud.title: Go nested with make:controller --crud
go-nested-with-make-controller-crud.description: Learn how the controller-first workflow behaves when the resource is nested and how that changes the generated routes, files, and prompts.

flat-or-nest-with-the-m-option.title: Flat or Nest with the ``-m`` Option
flat-or-nest-with-the-m-option.description: Learn what the structure choice means inside the controller-first workflow so you can pick the layout that matches your app instead of accepting a default blindly.

choose-flat-for-one-multi-word-model.title: Choose Flat for One Multi-Word Model
choose-flat-for-one-multi-word-model.description: Learn how --flat keeps a multi-word controller resource together as one model-backed structure when the words describe a single thing.

combine-namespaces-with-nested-model-gen.title: Combine Namespaces with Nested Model Generation
combine-namespaces-with-nested-model-gen.description: Learn how controller namespaces and nested model generation can work together when part of the name organizes the app and part describes data relationships.

build-nested-resources-one-level-at-a-ti.title: Build Nested Resources One Level at a Time (make:controller)
build-nested-resources-one-level-at-a-ti.description: Learn why building nested controller resources from the top down keeps generated parents, children, routes, and prompts easier to reason about.

intro-to-flask-make-model.title: Intro To Flask Make Model
intro-to-flask-make-model.description: Learn when a model-first workflow is the clearest starting point and how make:model can grow outward into the rest of the application structure.

make-a-basic-model.title: Make a basic model
make-a-basic-model.description: Learn how to generate a model first when the data structure is the clearest starting point for the feature you are building.

what-the-model-includes.title: What the model includes
what-the-model-includes.description: Learn what Flask-Commands puts into the generated model file so you know which parts are ready immediately and which parts you still need to shape yourself.

edit-the-model-and-migrate-the-database.title: Edit the model and migrate the database
edit-the-model-and-migrate-the-database.description: Learn the next practical step after generation so your model changes become real database structure instead of just code on disk.

create-update-and-delete-a-recipe.title: Create, Update, and Delete a Recipe
create-update-and-delete-a-recipe.description: Learn how to use the generated model methods in a Flask shell to create, update, and delete recipe records after the database schema is ready.

build-a-resource-with-make-model-crud.title: Build a resource with make:model --crud
build-a-resource-with-make-model-crud.description: Learn how a model-first command can expand outward into a fuller resource by generating the controller, routes, and templates around the data structure.

choose-flat-or-nested-with-crud-for-make.title: Choose Flat or Nested with ``--crud``
choose-flat-or-nested-with-crud-for-make.description: Learn how make:model --crud handles a multi-word model name when it could represent either one flat resource or a nested model chain.

skipping-the-prompt-with--flat-or--nest.title: Skipping the Prompt with ``--flat`` or ``--nest``
skipping-the-prompt-with--flat-or--nest.description: Learn how to bypass the interactive structure prompt when you already know whether the generated resource should be flat or nested.

choosing-flat-for-one-multi-word-model.title: Choosing Flat for One Multi-Word Model
choosing-flat-for-one-multi-word-model.description: Learn how --flat keeps a model name like ShoppingList together and generates the matching controller, routes, templates, and URL shape.

choosing-nest-for-parent-child-resource.title: Choosing Nest for a Parent-Child Resource
choosing-nest-for-parent-child-resource.description: Learn how --nest turns a name like RecipeIngredient into a child resource under Recipe, including the nested controller, route package, and URL shape.

use-make-controller-for-namespacing.title: Use ``make:controller`` for Namespacing
use-make-controller-for-namespacing.description: Learn why namespaces are controller and route organization rather than model structure, and why make:controller is the clearer tool for that job.

build-nested-resources-one-level-at-a-ti.title: Build Nested Resources One Level at a Time (make:model)
build-nested-resources-one-level-at-a-ti.description: Learn how to grow nested model-first resources from the top down so each registered parent is available before adding the next child.
